source: Titles and durations from the UI mockup. Card text is a DRAFT based on widely used self-help skills (paced breathing, 5-4-3-2-1 grounding, STOP, DBT TIP, urge surfing). It must be reviewed and approved by the project psychiatrist before any real use.

cards.title: Paced breathing
cards.intro: Breathing out for longer than you breathe in helps your body slow down. Follow the circle.
steps: Sit or stand however is comfortable. You can keep your eyes open.
Breathe in gently through your nose while the circle grows, for 4 seconds.
Breathe out slowly through your mouth while the circle shrinks, for 6 seconds.
Keep going for about 2 minutes. If counting feels hard, just follow the circle.

cards.title: 5-4-3-2-1 grounding
cards.intro: This brings your attention back to the room around you, one sense at a time. Take your time with each step.
steps: Name 5 things you can see.
Name 4 things you can feel, like your feet on the floor or the chair behind you.
Name 3 things you can hear.
Name 2 things you can smell, or two smells you like.
Name 1 thing you can taste, or one thing you like about yourself.

cards.title: STOP
cards.intro: A short pause before you act on a strong feeling.
steps: S: Stop. Don't act yet. Stay still for a moment.
T: Take a breath. One slow breath in, and a longer breath out.
O: Observe. What are you feeling, and where in your body? What is happening around you?
P: Proceed with something that helps. Ask: what would make the next ten minutes a little easier?

cards.title: TIP
cards.intro: For when feelings are very intense. These change your body quickly, which can make the feeling easier to ride out.
steps: T: Temperature. Splash cold water on your face, or hold something cold against your face for 30 seconds.
I: Intense movement. Move quickly for a minute: walk fast, march on the spot or climb stairs.
P: Paced breathing. Breathe out for longer than you breathe in, for a few minutes.
P: Paired muscle relaxation. Tense your hands and shoulders as you breathe in, then let them go as you breathe out.
cards.caution: Skip the cold water and fast movement if you have a heart condition, an eating disorder or a medical reason to avoid them. Use paced breathing instead.

cards.title: Urge surfing
cards.intro: Urges rise, peak and fall, like a wave. You don't have to act on one to make it pass.
steps: Notice the urge. Name it to yourself: "I'm having an urge to…"
Find where you feel it in your body. Is it tight, hot, restless?
Rate how strong it is, from 0 to 10.
Breathe slowly and watch it, like a wave, without pushing it away.
After a few minutes, rate it again. Most urges get weaker within minutes.

cards.title: Reach out
cards.intro: You don't have to explain everything. A short message to someone you trust is enough.
steps: Think of one person who is safe to contact: a friend, family member or colleague.
Send the message below, or write your own.
If no one answers, you can still talk to our care team or call a support line.
cards.message: I'm having a hard time right now. Could you call me or come and be with me for a bit?
